summary: In tonight's edition: A new law expanding the conditions for a constitutional referendum has ignited political tensions in DR Congo. summary: South Africa's ruling ANC party suffers its worst-ever local election results, securing just 30 percent of the vote, as coalition talks loom. summary: Two thousand tonnes of waste are dumped every day at the Dandora landfill site in the Kenyan capital Nairobi. summary: Thousands of Arab Sudanese who have arrived in Chad after fleeing fighting at home are facing mistrust and hostility from fellow Sudanese refugees. FRANCE 24's Harold Girard reports.

Economists warned against "alarmist" reactions to the exclusion and argue the broader economic fallout will likely be limited.

summary: In tonight's edition: Rwanda and South Africa will lose their duty-free access to the US market after being excluded from the AGOA trade programme. title: Diwali: Over one billion people mark victory of light over darkness
summary: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. In Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama, the deity celebrated during the festival, festivities included performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.

title: New Zealand's knife-edge parliamentary election delivers no clear winner
summary: No clear winner was produced in New Zealand’s legislative elections Saturday, setting up the two main blocs – Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition and opposition leader Chris Hipkins' left-wing alliance – for weeks of political wrangling to attempt to cobble together a majority. Hipkins said that while New Zealanders had spoken, "it may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you've said".

title: China keeps a close eye on US midterm shake-up
summary: The US midterm elections have resulted in the Democratic Party taking control of both chambers of the US Congress, leaving Donald Trump as a lame duck president for the remainder of his term. Professor Steve Tsang of the SOAS China Institute tells FRANCE 24 that, while a weakened Trump could strengthen Beijing's negotiating position, the Chinese leadership is aware that Congress has relatively little sway over foreign policy and is keen to maintain warm personal ties between the two presidents.

title: Pollution, shortages, crime: Daily life in Pakistan's megacity Karachi
summary: Fed up with hours of power cuts, the residents of Pakistan's economic hub Karachi took to the streets in recent days and blocked several major roads. The outburst of anger highlights the daily problems faced by a megacity of over 21 million people, which has once again been ranked among the world's least liveable cities.

title: South Korea pushes digital detox for young people addicted to screens
summary: Back in August, France's Constitutional Council overturned a social media ban for children under 15. Some students, though, are now banned from using their smartphones at school. title: Food safety in India: A challenge for the world's most populous country

The country has witnessed a rise in cases of food adulteration, with sometimes fatal consequences. As concerns over adulteration and poor hygiene grow, questions are being raised about whether regulators can effectively oversee such a sprawling sector.

title: Hong Kong leader apologises and housing minister resigns after fire investigation exposes failures
